name: MonarchUsernameAvailabilityInput
title: UsernameAvailabilityInput
wrapsNative: TextField with .task(id:) for the debounced check
summary: A labelled text field whose value is checked while the person types, with the status shown as an icon and a message and announced.
whenToUse: For handles, workspace addresses and slugs that must be unique.
whenNotToUse: For validation that needs no request, use MonarchTextField with its error parameter.
api: init(_ label: String, text: Binding<String>, prompt: String? = nil, helper: String? = nil, prefix: String? = nil, isRequired: Bool = false, debounce: Duration = .milliseconds(400), checkingLabel: String? = nil, validLabel: String? = nil, invalidLabel: String? = nil, errorLabel: String? = nil, retryLabel: String? = nil, transform: ((String) -> String)? = nil, onStatusChange: (@MainActor (MonarchUsernameAvailabilityStatus, String?) -> Void)? = nil, validate: @escaping @Sendable (String) async throws -> MonarchUsernameAvailabilityResult?)
struct MonarchUsernameAvailabilityResult { init(isValid: Bool, message: String? = nil) }
enum MonarchUsernameAvailabilityStatus { case idle, checking, valid, invalid, error }

options.name: text
options.description: The text to edit and check.

options.name: prompt
options.description: Placeholder shown while the field is empty.

options.name: helper
options.description: Supporting text under the field, shown while there is no status message.

options.name: prefix
options.description: Fixed text before the value, such as a domain.

options.name: debounce
options.description: How long typing must pause before the check runs.

options.name: transform
options.description: Rewrites typed text before it is stored, such as lower-casing.

options.name: onStatusChange
options.description: Runs when the status or its message changes.

options.name: validate
options.description: The check. Return nil when there is nothing to check. Throwing sets the error status.

options.name: isRequired
options.description: Shows the required mark after the label.

states.name: idle
states.description: A plain field; the helper text shows.

states.name: checking
states.description: A progress indicator at the end of the field and "Checking availability…" under it.

states.name: valid
states.description: A success border, a check symbol and the message in the success colour.

states.name: invalid
states.description: A danger border, a warning symbol and the message in the danger colour.

states.name: error
states.description: An information symbol in the warning colour, the message and a "Try again" button.

states.name: focused
states.description: Draws the theme's focus ring around the field.

states.name: disabled
states.description: Subtle background and the disabled text colour, set with disabled(_:).

appearance: The same field as MonarchTextField, with the prefix in the muted text colour before the text and the status icon after it.
platformNotes: The web passes an AbortSignal to the check; here the check runs in a task that SwiftUI cancels when the text changes, which also cancels URLSession requests made in it. The web has sm, md and lg sizes; iOS has the one size of MonarchTextField. The web reports the first idle status on mount; onStatusChange runs on changes only. Monarch does no networking. Several closures are optional (transform, onStatusChange). Pass each one with its label: Swift gives a single unlabelled trailing closure to the first parameter that accepts it, which is transform.
accessibility: The field is one VoiceOver element: label, value, and a hint made of the prefix, the helper text and the status message.
Settled results ("Available", "Not available", a failure) are announced; "Checking" is not.
Each status has its own icon and message, not colour alone.
The "Try again" button is a separate element with a 44-point touch target.
The field is at least 44 points high and the whole field focuses the input.
edgeCases: Empty text is idle and is never checked.
A check cancelled by new typing never writes its result, so the status always describes the latest text.
"Try again" runs the check at once, without the wait.
The message returned by the check replaces the built-in and overridden texts.
Changing validate does not start a new check; the next edit does.

examples.title: Workspace address
examples.code:
MonarchUsernameAvailabilityInput(
    "Workspace address",
    text: $address,
    prompt: "your-team",
    helper: "Try “team” to see a taken address.",
    prefix: "example.com/",
    isRequired: true
) { address in
    MonarchUsernameAvailabilityResult(isValid: !["admin", "help", "support", "team"].contains(address))
}

examples.title: Lower-casing and blocking submit until valid
examples.code:
MonarchUsernameAvailabilityInput(
    "Workspace address",
    text: $slug,
    helper: "Letters, numbers and dashes.",
    transform: { $0.lowercased() },
    onStatusChange: { status, _ in canSubmit = status == .valid },
    validate: { slug in
        slug.count < 3
            ? MonarchUsernameAvailabilityResult(isValid: false, message: "Use at least 3 characters.")
            : MonarchUsernameAvailabilityResult(isValid: true)
    }
)
MonarchButton("Create", variant: .primary) {}
    .disabled(!canSubmit)
examples.setup:
@State private var slug = ""
@State private var canSubmit = false
